candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest assigns a 0.83 malware probability, but the supplied evidence is weak and mostly generic. Of the top 20 n-grams, 18 push toward cryptojacking and 2 toward benign (CMP JNZ at -0.013385 and CALL MOV at -0.008494). Most of the positive contributions come from very common compiler-generated patterns: MOV LEAVE (+0.012767), LEAVE RET (+0.008498), ADD PUSH (+0.012371), PUSH MOV (+0.011623), MOV PUSH (+0.011336), POP PUSH (+0.009381) and POP MOV (+0.008216). These reflect ordinary function prologue/epilogue and stack handling, not mining behavior. Twelve of the 20 n-grams have a frequency of 0.000000 in this binary (ADD POP, CMOVZ MOV, XOR MOV, CALL ADD, PUSH SUB, XOR CALL, XOR XOR, CMP JZ, XOR CMOVNZ, XOR SHL, LEA CALL). Their positive SHAP values therefore come from the model treating their absence as a signal, which is not direct evidence of any mining routine. The XOR-heavy n-grams (XOR XOR, XOR SHL, XOR CMOVNZ, XOR MOV, XOR CALL) are the kind of bitwise mixing often seen in hashing or crypto code, but they are absent here, so they cannot be taken as evidence of such code. No function-level locations or distinctive mining-related constructs are provided. The evidence is therefore consistent with the model's leaning toward malware but does not substantiate cryptojacking, so the result is inconclusive.
